Xiaomi thermal files in /vendor/etc/thermal-*.conf are encrypted with AES-128-CBC for mi_thermald. When you open a file here, it is automatically decrypted for editing. When you tap Save & Apply, it is re-encrypted and applied as an override in /data/vendor/thermal/config/, and mi_thermald is restarted. Original stock files in /vendor/etc/ are never modified.

Each section in [BRACKETS] defines a virtual sensor or a throttling rule:
• algo_type: algorithm (ss = clock throttling, monitor = stepped actions, Virtual = combined sensor)
• sensor: monitored sensor (usually VIRTUAL-SENSOR0 or battery)
• device: controlled component (cpu0 = Little, cpu4 = Big, cpu7 = Prime, gpu, battery, lcd)
• polling: check interval in milliseconds (1000 = 1 second)

Temperatures are in millidegrees Celsius (m°C): 40000 = 40 °C, 45000 = 45 °C, 48000 = 48 °C.
• trig: temperature at which the limit activates.
• clr: temperature at which the limit clears (must always be lower than its matching trig).
• Keep values in ascending order and make sure trig, clr, and target have the exact same number of columns separated by tabs.

• CPU (cpu0, cpu4, cpu7): frequencies in kHz (e.g. 1766400 = 1766 MHz, 2227200 = 2227 MHz). Always use valid frequencies supported by the cluster.\n• GPU (gpu): frequency or level matching the original format of that file.\n• Battery (battery): charging current limit levels (higher level = lower charging current).

• Raise temperature thresholds gradually (2–3 °C at a time) and monitor battery temperature.\n• Never disable thermal protection completely — excessive heat can degrade the battery or cause thermal shutdown.\n• If anything behaves unexpectedly, tap Reset on the file (or Reset all overrides) to return immediately to stock.

Comută reglajele de stocare I/O și rețea TCP

Power Preset quickly switches between stock (Default), power-saving (Battery), and maximum performance (Gaming). Enable Apply on boot only after confirming your settings are stable. Use Reset to defaults anytime to return to stock values.

Input Boost raises clocks briefly on touch (higher = smoother scrolling, more battery). WALT Profile controls how quickly frequencies scale up and down. Limit Prime Core caps the Cortex-X2 core to reduce heat. Top-App Uclamp sets the CPU reservation for the foreground app. Little handles light tasks, Big handles main workloads, and Prime handles peak bursts.

Lowering max GPU frequency reduces heat and saves battery; raising min frequency can reduce frame drops at the cost of power. msm-adreno-tz is the balanced default governor. Adreno Idler drops GPU clock faster when idle to save battery. Lower Idle Timer saves power; higher values (80–100 ms) keep clocks steady in games.

ZRAM compresses inactive RAM to keep more apps in memory (0 disables it). lz4 and lzo-rle are fastest with lowest CPU use; zstd compresses more tightly using extra CPU. Higher Swappiness moves idle pages to ZRAM sooner. Lower VFS Cache Pressure keeps file cache longer. Page Cluster 0 is recommended for ZRAM. Dirty Writeback balances latency (10/5) vs bulk write speed (40/20).

Storage I/O Scheduler orders disk requests: mq-deadline and none give lowest latency on UFS flash, kyber balances latency, and bfq favors smooth multitasking. Read-Ahead (read_ahead_kb) controls how much extra data is prefetched: 128–256 KB is snappier for random reads and app launches, while 512–2048 KB improves large sequential reads and media playback.

TCP Congestion Control manages how network packets scale with bandwidth and loss. bbr typically lowers latency and improves throughput on mobile or unstable networks; cubic is the balanced Linux default; reno is more conservative.
